title: Self performance heuristics — quick reference (Ryan Cho)
content:
Purpose:
A short, scrappy reference I can use during prep for 1:1s, calibration threads, and my next self-review. The goal is to capture short heuristics, quick evidence snippets, and one-line asks so I can stitch them into narratives rapidly.

---

Core heuristics (one-liners):
- Signal over story: start with the concrete metric or outcome, then add the behavioral story. If I can’t name the measurable impact in one sentence, it’s not ready.
- 2x evidence rule: for each claim, have 2 independent evidence snippets (different projects, stakeholders, or timestamps).
- Timeline anchor: always pair results with when they happened (QX, month). Timing anchors help calibration.
- Confidence tiers: label statements as: observed-fact / inferred-pattern / hypothesis. Use inferred/hypothesis sparingly during calibration.
- Micro-metrics > vague adjectives: prefer numbers (latency %, adoption count, reduced ops pages) to adjectives ("improved", "better").

Quick signal scaffolding (templates to capture fast):
- Outcome: "Reduced median inference latency from 420ms -> 160ms (P50) for host/api by Q3 2025."
- Contribution: "Led kernel selection testing and rollout canary for model X, coordinated infra + runtime teams (3 engs) over 6 weeks."
- Stakeholder impact: "Enabled product team to ship feature Y on schedule; saved ~250 engineering-hours in post-launch support."
- Evidence links: Confluence, PR, dashboard id (put each on a separate line).

Example evidence snippets (copyable):
- "Dashboard: /dash/perf/model-x/p50 — shows P50 drop from 420 to 160 between 2025-06-10 and 2025-07-18; controlled canary on 3 nodes. (link: confluence:PERF-MODELX-2025)",
- "PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1421 — kernel change + test plan; reviewers: @maya, @li. (merged 2025-07-12)",
- "Support log: pagerduty incident #3245 — 0 post-rollout pages for release window (vs baseline 4/month)."

Behavioral story arcs (short):
- Problem -> Action -> Clarifying signal -> Outcome. Keep each section to 1 sentence.
  Example: "We consistently missed P50 targets (problem). I ran A/B kernel selection and small-batch tests with infra (action), which revealed a config bias at 128 tokens (signal). After rolling selective kernels we hit P50 SLO and reduced pages (outcome)."

Manager prep bullet set (top of any thread I send):
- Context (1 line): what I was trying to accomplish and why it mattered to the org.
- What I did (1-2 lines): my direct contributions and coordination.
- Clear metric(s) (1 line): concrete numbers and timeframe.
- What I learned / tradeoffs (1 line): assumptions, risks, what I’d do differently.
- Asks (1 line each): e.g., "Request promotion calibration", "Headcount to own feature Z", "Approval to run cross-team experiment".

Ask templates (pick one depending on ask type):
- Promotion calibration: "I’d like calibration for a promotion to [level]. Key signals: impact X (metric), leadership Y (number of teams), scope Z (systems owned). Can we schedule a 20-min calibration?"
- Resource ask: "Request approval for 0.5 FTE for 3 months to own rollout automation; expected benefit: 30% fewer post-rollout rollbacks (estimate)."
- Time/priority ask: "I need to deprioritize project A to complete B; consequence: A slips by 2 weeks, B avoids a 3-week outage window."

Calibration red flags (things to call out early):
- Single-source evidence (only one PR or one stakeholder).
- Hand-wavy metrics (no baseline, no timeframe).
- Conflicting stakeholder signals (eng says yes, product says no).
- Overclaiming ownership (used team credit instead of "led/partnered with").

Micro-metrics catalog (examples to pull from dashboards quickly):
- Latency: P50, P95, tail (ms) by model and route.
- Cost: $/token or $/1000 requests pre/post change.
- Ops load: pages/month, mean time to resolve.
- Adoption: percentage of routes using config X, number of customers on dedicated capacity.

Snippets to paste into a one-pager (pick 2–3):
- "Impact: Reduced P50 by 62% for model-X route; empirically reduced paging by 100% during the 6-week post-rollout window."
- "Ownership: Led cross-functional canary (runtime + infra + product); accountable for rollout gating and rollback plan."
- "Learned: Kernel tuning provided diminishing returns past 6 weeks; better ROI coming from targeted quantization for heavy routes."

Open questions / next actions (personal TO-DOs):
- Pull final dashboard exports for Q4 2025 (dash ids: perf/model-x, cost/route).
- Ask Maya for reviewer notes on PR #1421; store a 1-paragraph summary.
- Draft promotion blurb (150 words) using the above templates and circulate to manager 1 week before calibration.

One-line prompts for quick thinking (use as mental checklist in prep):
- "Can I state the numeric impact in one sentence?"
- "Do I have at least 2 independent evidence items?"
- "Who else needs to see this before calibration?"

Quick archiving convention (my personal habit):
- Title: "2025-Q3 — [project short] — 1-line impact". Put links to confluence + PR in the first paragraph. Save a one-paragraph summary in personal drive under the same naming.

Last quick note: keep this intentionally short and messy. The real work is in capturing the signal now, polishing later. If something feels "too pretty", it probably needs more evidence.

\\
(End of scratchpad)
